source.text: בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לְצֵ֥את בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה בָּ֖אוּ מִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: In the month the third of [the] going out of [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt, on the day the this they came [to the] wilderness of Sinai.

en.L: In the third month of the going out of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the land of Egypt, on this day they came [to] the wilderness of Sinai.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the day the third month began after their departure from the land of Egypt.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} reached the Desert of Sinai at the start of the third month after they left Egypt.

es.L: En el mes tercero de la salida de los hijos de Israel de la tierra de Egipto, en este día, llegaron [al] desierto del Sinaí.
es.B: Los israelitas llegaron al desierto del Sinaí el día en que comenzaba el tercer mes después de su salida de la tierra de Egipto.
es.R: Los israelitas llegaron al desierto del Sinaí al principio del tercer mes después de salir de Egipto.

fr.L: Au troisième mois de la sortie des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël du pays d’Égypte, ce jour-là, ils arrivèrent [au] désert du Sinaï.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} arrivèrent au désert du Sinaï le jour où commençait le troisième mois après leur départ du pays d’Égypte.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} sont arrivés au désert du Sinaï au début du troisième mois après leur sortie d’Égypte.

sw.L: Katika mwezi wa tatu tangu kutoka kwa wana wa Israeli katika nchi ya Misri, siku hiyo hiyo walifika [katika] jangwa la Sinai.
sw.B: Waisraeli walifika katika jangwa la Sinai siku ile mwezi wa tatu ulipoanza tangu walipotoka katika nchi ya Misri.
sw.R: Waisraeli walifika katika jangwa la Sinai mwanzoni mwa mwezi wa tatu baada ya kutoka Misri.

vi.L: Vào tháng thứ ba sau khi con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập, chính ngày ấy, họ đến hoang mạc Si-na-i.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đến hoang mạc Si-na-i vào ngày đầu tháng thứ ba kể từ khi họ ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đến hoang mạc Si-na-i vào đầu tháng thứ ba sau khi họ rời Ai Cập.

ko.L: 이스라엘 자손이 이집트 땅에서 나온 지 셋째 달, 바로 이날에 그들이 시내 광야에 이르렀다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성은 이집트 땅을 떠난 지 셋째 달 첫날에 시내 광야에 이르렀다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 이집트를 떠난 지 셋째 달이 시작되는 날에 시내 광야에 도착했다.

pt.L: No terceiro mês da saída dos filhos de Israel da terra do Egito, neste dia, eles chegaram ao deserto do Sinai.
pt.B: Os israelitas chegaram ao deserto do Sinai no dia em que começava o terceiro mês depois da sua saída da terra do Egito.
pt.R: Os israelitas chegaram ao deserto do Sinai no começo do terceiro mês depois de terem saído do Egito.

decisions.choice: in the third month ... on this day: on the first day of the third month
alternatives: in the third month ... on that same day (with no exact day given)
decisions.reason: The word for "month" also means "new moon", the day a month begins. "On this day" then points to that day: the new moon of the third month after leaving Egypt. Israel left on the fifteenth day of the first month (12:6, 31; Numbers 33:3), so about six weeks had passed.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Sinai: the desert land around Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: The name covers the wild land around the mountain where Israel will camp until Numbers 10:11-12. The mountain is the place where God met Moses in the bush (3:1, 12), there called Horeb.

decisions.choice: Desert of Sinai
decisions.reason: Readable says "desert" for "wilderness", as it says "Desert of Sin" (16:1; 17:1).

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("ils arrivèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("ils sont arrivés")
decisions.reason: French written narrative uses the passé simple; Readable uses the passé composé of everyday French, as docs/french-style.md sets for every narrative passage. God's words in this chapter keep the tenses of speech.

decisions.choice: "시내 광야", "시내 산"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's Protestant form of the name, used through these books.

decisions.choice: "Si-na-i"
decisions.reason: The form the project's New Testament uses (Acts 7; Galatians 4), kept through the Pentateuch so the two agree.

decisions.choice: o deserto do Sinai
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Portuguese names the region with the article, "do Sinai", as it says "o monte Sinai"; "deserto" serves for "wilderness" at every level, as the terms list sets it, so Readable needs no other word where the English Readable says "Desert".

source.text: וַיִּסְע֣וּ מֵרְפִידִ֗ים וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ מִדְבַּ֣ר סִינַ֔י וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיִּֽחַן־שָׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נֶ֥גֶד הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Rephidim and they came [to the] wilderness of Sinai and they encamped in the wilderness, and encamped there Israel before the mountain.

en.L: And they set out from Rephidim and came [to] the wilderness of Sinai, and they camped in the wilderness; and Israel camped there before the mountain.
en.B: They had moved on from Rephidim and come into the wilderness of Sinai, and there in the wilderness they set up camp. Israel camped there, facing the mountain.
en.R: They had left Rephidim and come into the Desert of Sinai. They set up camp there in the desert, with Israel's tents facing the mountain.

es.L: Y partieron de Refidim y llegaron [al] desierto del Sinaí, y acamparon en el desierto; y acampó allí Israel frente al monte.
es.B: Habían salido de Refidim y entrado en el desierto del Sinaí, y allí en el desierto levantaron su campamento. Israel acampó allí, frente al monte.
es.R: Habían salido de Refidim y entrado en el desierto del Sinaí. Allí en el desierto montaron su campamento, con las tiendas de Israel frente al monte.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de Rephidim et arrivèrent [au] désert du Sinaï, et ils campèrent dans le désert ; et Israël campa là, en face de la montagne.
fr.B: Ils étaient partis de Rephidim et étaient entrés dans le désert du Sinaï, et ils établirent leur camp là, dans le désert. Israël campa là, face à la montagne.
fr.R: Ils avaient quitté Rephidim et ils étaient entrés dans le désert du Sinaï. Ils ont installé leur camp là, dans le désert, et les tentes d’Israël faisaient face à la montagne.

sw.L: Nao wakasafiri kutoka Refidimu, wakafika [katika] jangwa la Sinai, wakapiga kambi jangwani; naye Israeli akapiga kambi huko mbele ya mlima.
sw.B: Walikuwa wameondoka Refidimu na kuingia katika jangwa la Sinai, nao wakapiga kambi pale jangwani. Waisraeli walipiga kambi huko, wakiukabili mlima.
sw.R: Walikuwa wameondoka Refidimu na kuingia katika jangwa la Sinai. Walipiga kambi pale jangwani, na mahema ya Israeli yakaelekea mlima.

vi.L: Và họ ra đi từ Rê-phi-đim và đến hoang mạc Si-na-i, và họ đóng trại trong hoang mạc; và Y-sơ-ra-ên đóng trại tại đó, trước núi.
vi.B: Họ đã rời Rê-phi-đim và đến hoang mạc Si-na-i, rồi đóng trại trong hoang mạc. Y-sơ-ra-ên đóng trại tại đó, đối diện với núi.
vi.R: Họ đã rời Rê-phi-đim và vào hoang mạc Si-na-i. Họ dựng trại tại đó trong hoang mạc, các lều của Y-sơ-ra-ên quay mặt về phía núi.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 르비딤을 떠나 시내 광야에 이르러 광야에 진을 쳤다. 그리고 이스라엘이 거기 산 앞에 진을 쳤다.
ko.B: 그들은 르비딤을 떠나 시내 광야로 들어가, 그 광야에 진을 쳤다. 이스라엘은 거기 산을 마주하고 진을 쳤다.
ko.R: 그들은 르비딤을 떠나 시내 광야로 들어갔다. 그들은 그 광야에 진을 쳤는데, 이스라엘의 장막들은 산을 바라보고 있었다.

pt.L: E partiram de Refidim e chegaram ao deserto do Sinai e acamparam no deserto; e Israel acampou ali diante do monte.
pt.B: Eles tinham partido de Refidim e chegado ao deserto do Sinai, e ali no deserto armaram o acampamento. Israel acampou ali, de frente para o monte.
pt.R: Eles tinham saído de Refidim e chegado ao deserto do Sinai. Ali no deserto montaram o acampamento, com as tendas de Israel viradas para o monte.

decisions.choice: Israel camped: the whole people as one
decisions.reason: After the plural "they camped", the verse switches to a singular verb with "Israel" as its subject. The people camp as one body before the mountain, ready for what God will do there.

decisions.choice: before the mountain: the mountain of God
decisions.reason: "The mountain" needs no name: it is the mountain of God where Moses was told that Israel would serve God (3:1, 12). That promise is now being kept.

decisions.choice: with Israel's tents facing the mountain
decisions.reason: Readable turns "Israel camped there before the mountain" into a picture of the camp's tents facing it; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: "naye Israeli akapiga kambi" (singular)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew switch to a singular verb with "Israel" as subject (the people camping as one body); Balanced and Readable use the plural "Waisraeli".

decisions.choice: o monte (and "o monte Sinai", verse 11)
decisions.reason: "Monte" is the Portuguese word for a mountain where God meets his people ("o monte Sinai", "o monte de Deus"), the word Matthew 5:1 also uses in Portuguese and Exodus 3:1 uses for "o monte de Deus"; "a montanha" is the ordinary geographic word and reads as scenery. Lowercase "monte" before the name, as Portuguese writes "o monte Sinai".

source.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֥ה עָלָ֖ה אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ מִן־הָהָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֤ה תֹאמַר֙ לְבֵ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְתַגֵּ֖יד לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And Moses went up to the God, and called to him Yahweh from the mountain saying, thus you will say to [the] house of Jacob and you will tell to [the] sons of Israel,

en.L: And Moses went up to God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called to him from the mountain, saying, "Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and tell to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel:
en.B: Moses went up to God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called out to him from the mountain: "Say this to the house of Jacob, and declare it to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}:
en.R: Moses went up the mountain to meet with God. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called to him from the mountain and said, "Here is what you must tell the family of Jacob, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}:

es.L: Y Moisés subió a Dios, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo llamó desde el monte, diciendo: «Así dirás a la casa de Jacob y anunciarás a los hijos de Israel:
es.B: Moisés subió hacia Dios, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo llamó desde el monte: «Di esto a la casa de Jacob, y declara a los israelitas:
es.R: Moisés subió al monte para encontrarse con Dios. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo llamó desde el monte y le dijo: «Esto es lo que debes decir a la familia de Jacob, a los israelitas:

fr.L: Et Moïse monta vers Dieu, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’appela de la montagne, disant : « Ainsi tu diras à la maison de Jacob, et tu annonceras aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël :
fr.B: Moïse monta vers Dieu, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’appela depuis la montagne : « Voici ce que tu diras à la maison de Jacob, ce que tu déclareras aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} :
fr.R: Moïse est monté sur la montagne pour rencontrer Dieu. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a appelé de la montagne et lui a dit : « Voici ce que tu dois dire à la famille de Jacob, aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} :

sw.L: Naye Musa akapanda kwa Mungu, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwita kutoka mlimani, akisema, "Hivi ndivyo utakavyoiambia nyumba ya Yakobo, na kuwaeleza wana wa Israeli:
sw.B: Musa alipanda kwenda kwa Mungu, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwita kutoka mlimani: "Iambie nyumba ya Yakobo haya, uwatangazie Waisraeli:
sw.R: Musa alipanda mlimani ili kukutana na Mungu. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwita kutoka mlimani, akamwambia, "Haya ndiyo utakayowaambia jamaa ya Yakobo, yaani Waisraeli:

vi.L: Và Môi-se đi lên cùng Đức Chúa Trời, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} gọi ông từ trên núi mà phán: "Ngươi hãy nói như vầy với nhà Gia-cốp và bảo cho con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên:
vi.B: Môi-se lên gặp Đức Chúa Trời, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} từ trên núi gọi ông mà phán: "Con hãy nói điều này với nhà Gia-cốp và tuyên bố cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên:
vi.R: Môi-se đi lên núi để gặp Đức Chúa Trời. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} từ trên núi gọi ông và phán: "Đây là điều con phải nói với gia đình Gia-cốp, tức là dân Y-sơ-ra-ên:

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 하나님께로 올라갔는데, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 산에서 그를 부르며 말씀하셨다. "너는 야곱의 집에 이렇게 말하고 이스라엘 자손에게 알려라.
ko.B: 모세가 하나님께로 올라가자, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 산에서 그를 부르셨다. "야곱의 집에 이렇게 말하고, 이스라엘 백성에게 이렇게 전하여라.
ko.R: 모세는 하나님을 만나러 산으로 올라갔다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 산에서 그를 부르시며 말씀하셨다. "야곱의 집안, 곧 이스라엘 사람들에게 이렇게 전하여라.

pt.L: E Moisés subiu a Deus, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o chamou do monte, dizendo: "Assim dirás à casa de Jacó e anunciarás aos filhos de Israel:
pt.B: Moisés subiu até Deus, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o chamou do monte: "Isto é o que dirás à casa de Jacó e anunciarás aos israelitas:
pt.R: Moisés subiu o monte para se encontrar com Deus. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} o chamou do monte e disse: "Isto é o que deves dizer à família de Jacó, aos israelitas:

decisions.choice: Moses went up to God ... from the mountain: Moses climbs toward God, who calls to him from the mountain
decisions.reason: Moses goes up toward the place where God is present, and God speaks to him from the mountain before he reaches the top. This is the first of several climbs in chapters 19-24.

decisions.choice: the house of Jacob ... the sons of Israel: the same people, named twice
decisions.reason: The two names stand in parallel, as in poetry. "House of Jacob" recalls the family that went down to Egypt (1:1); "sons of Israel" is the people as a nation. The words that follow are formal and carefully shaped.

decisions.choice: went up the mountain to meet with God
decisions.reason: Readable says where Moses went and why. The Hebrew has "went up to God".

source.text: אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי לְמִצְרָ֑יִם וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶתְכֶם֙ עַל־כַּנְפֵ֣י נְשָׁרִ֔ים וָאָבִ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: You you have seen what I did to Egypt, and I carried you on wings of eagles and I brought you to myself.

en.L: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and [how] I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}.
en.B: 'You saw with your own eyes what I did to the Egyptians, and how I lifted you up on eagles' wings and brought you here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: 'You saw what I did to the Egyptians. I carried you along the way an eagle carries its young on its wings, and I brought you here to be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: “{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:han visto|habéis visto}} lo que hice a Egipto, y [cómo] {{plural_you:los|os}} llevé sobre alas de águilas y {{plural_you:los|os}} traje a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: “{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} con {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} propios ojos lo que hice a los egipcios, y cómo {{plural_you:los|os}} levanté sobre alas de águilas y {{plural_you:los|os}} traje aquí, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: “{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:vieron|visteis}} lo que hice a los egipcios. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} llevé por el camino como el águila lleva a sus crías sobre sus alas, y {{plural_you:los|os}} traje aquí para que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} conmigo.

fr.L: “Vous, vous avez vu ce que j’ai fait à l’Égypte, et [comment] je vous ai portés sur des ailes d’aigles et vous ai amenés à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: “Vous avez vu de vos propres yeux ce que j’ai fait aux Égyptiens, et comment je vous ai soulevés sur des ailes d’aigles pour vous amener ici, jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: “Vous avez vu ce que j’ai fait aux Égyptiens. Je vous ai portés tout au long du chemin, comme un aigle porte ses petits sur ses ailes, et je vous ai amenés ici pour que vous soyez avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: 'Ninyi wenyewe mmeona niliyoitendea Misri, na [jinsi] nilivyowachukua juu ya mabawa ya tai na kuwaleta {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.
sw.B: 'Mliona kwa macho yenu wenyewe niliyowatendea Wamisri, na jinsi nilivyowainua juu ya mabawa ya tai na kuwaleta hapa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.
sw.R: 'Mliona niliyowatendea Wamisri. Niliwabeba njiani kama tai anavyowabeba makinda yake juu ya mabawa yake, nikawaleta hapa ili mkae {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.

vi.L: 'Chính các ngươi đã thấy điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho Ai Cập, và [thể nào] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã cõng các ngươi trên cánh chim đại bàng và đem các ngươi đến với chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: 'Chính mắt các ngươi đã thấy điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cho người Ai Cập, và thể nào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nâng các ngươi trên cánh chim đại bàng mà đem các ngươi đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: 'Các ngươi đã thấy điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cho người Ai Cập. Ta đã mang các ngươi đi như chim đại bàng mang con mình trên cánh, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đem các ngươi đến đây để ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: '너희 자신이 내가 이집트에 한 일을 보았고, 내가 너희를 독수리들의 날개에 업어 나에게로 데려온 것을 [보았다].
ko.B: '내가 이집트 사람들에게 한 일을 너희가 직접 보았다. 내가 독수리 날개에 태우듯 너희를 업어 나에게로 데려온 것도 보았다.
ko.R: '너희는 내가 이집트 사람들에게 한 일을 보았다. 독수리가 새끼를 날개에 태우고 날듯이, 내가 너희를 업어서 여기 나에게로 데려왔다.

pt.L: 'Vocês mesmos viram o que eu fiz ao Egito, e [como] os carreguei sobre asas de águias e os trouxe a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.B: 'Vocês viram com os próprios olhos o que eu fiz aos egípcios, e como os levantei sobre asas de águias e os trouxe até aqui, para junto de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.R: 'Vocês viram o que eu fiz aos egípcios. Eu carreguei vocês pelo caminho como a águia carrega os filhotes nas suas asas, e trouxe vocês até aqui para ficarem {{deity_pronoun:comigo|Comigo}}.

decisions.choice: carried you on eagles' wings: God bore Israel safely and with strength
decisions.reason: The picture is of a great bird carrying its young. Deuteronomy 32:11-12 uses the same picture of the LORD guiding Israel through the wilderness. It speaks of God's power and care in bringing them out of Egypt and through the desert.

decisions.choice: eagles: large birds of prey, perhaps vultures
decisions.reason: The word names a large bird of prey. It can include the griffon vulture (Micah 1:16 speaks of its bald head). The point is the bird's size, strength and swift flight, not which bird it is.

decisions.choice: brought you to myself: God's goal was not only freedom but nearness to him
decisions.reason: The exodus was not only an escape from Egypt. God brought the people to the mountain where he is present, to belong to him and serve him (3:12; 6:7).

decisions.choice: vocês (God to Israel, plural here)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: where God speaks to Israel in the plural, as here (the Hebrew "you" is plural through verse 6), Portuguese says "vocês"; where he addresses Israel in the singular, as in the Ten Words (20:2-17) and many laws, "tu" (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md). decisions.choice: if you will surely listen to my voice: if you will truly obey me
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. To "listen to the voice" of someone is to do what they say (15:26; Deuteronomy 13:5). The promise that follows rests on Israel's keeping the covenant.

decisions.choice: possession: a personal treasure, specially owned and valued
decisions.reason: The word is used of a king's own store of treasure (1 Chronicles 29:3; Ecclesiastes 2:8). God uses it of Israel in Deuteronomy 7:6, 14:2 and 26:18, and Malachi 3:17 and 1 Peter 2:9 take it up. Israel belongs to God in a special way, though all peoples are his.

decisions.choice: for all the earth is mine: a reason, or a contrast
alternatives: although all the earth is mine
decisions.reason: The joining word usually means "for" or "because": God, who owns the whole earth, is free to choose one people as his own. It can also be read as "although": though the whole earth is his, Israel will be his in a special way. Both readings stress that Israel's place is God's choice, not their own claim.

decisions.choice: my own special treasure
decisions.reason: The word means property that is especially prized; "own special treasure" brings out both ownership and value. Literal has "special possession".

decisions.choice: "una posesión preciada" (L), "mi tesoro personal" (B), "mi propio tesoro" (R) for segullah
decisions.reason: Segullah is property that is both owned and prized. Literal says "posesión" with "preciada" for the value; Balanced and Readable say "tesoro" with "personal" / "propio" for the ownership.

decisions.choice: "un trésor particulier" (L), "mon propre trésor" (B), "mon trésor à moi" (R) for segullah
decisions.reason: Segullah is a personal treasure, both owned and prized (a king's own store, 1 Chronicles 29:3). "Trésor" keeps the value, and "particulier" / "propre" / "à moi" keep the ownership; "part" or "bien" would keep only the ownership.

decisions.choice: "milki ya pekee" (L), "hazina yangu ya pekee" (B, R) for segullah
decisions.reason: Segullah is a personal treasure, owned and prized, like a king's own treasury. "Hazina" says treasure kept and valued; Literal keeps the plainer "milki" (possession) with "ya pekee" (special). "Mali" alone would lose the sense of value.

decisions.choice: "특별한 소유" (L); "소중한 보물" (B); "특별한 보물" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a treasure owned and kept by its owner; Literal keeps "possession", Balanced and Readable say how highly it is valued.

decisions.choice: "언약" for covenant
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for covenant, used through the Old and New Testaments in Korean.

decisions.choice: "của riêng quý báu" (L); "báu vật riêng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is a personal treasure, specially owned and valued (meaning decision); "báu vật riêng" says both the owning and the value. "giao ước" is the term sheet's word for covenant.

decisions.choice: a aliança
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Genesis and the terms list: "aliança" is the word Brazilian readers know for God's covenant with Israel, and the word of "o Livro da Aliança" (24:7) and "o sangue da aliança" (24:8); "pacto" sounds like a contract between equals and "concerto" is archaic.

decisions.choice: a kingdom of priests: a people who all serve God as priests do
decisions.reason: A priest stands near God, serves him and brings others near to him. The whole people is to belong to God in this way and stand between him and the other peoples of the earth, whom he also owns (verse 5). 1 Peter 2:9 and Revelation 1:6 and 5:10 apply the words to the people of Christ.

decisions.choice: a holy nation: a nation set apart to belong to God
decisions.reason: "Holy" means set apart for God and marked by his character (Leviticus 11:44; 19:2). The word for "nation" is the one used of other peoples; Israel is a people among the nations but set apart from them.

decisions.choice: these are the words: the message Moses is to carry ends here
decisions.reason: The phrase closes the message begun in verse 3. Verses 7-8 tell how Moses passed it on and how the people answered.

decisions.choice: who serve me ... set apart for me
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what being priests and being holy means here. The Hebrew has "to me" once, covering both phrases.

decisions.choice: "제사장들의 나라", "거룩한 민족" (L, B); "따로 구별된 민족" (R)
decisions.reason: "민족" (nation, goy) is kept apart from "백성" (people, am), which this chapter uses for Israel gathered at the mountain.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc thầy tế lễ"; "dân tộc thánh"
decisions.reason: "thầy tế lễ" is the term sheet's word for priest, and "dân tộc thánh" is the phrase of the project's Vietnamese 1 Peter 2:9, which takes up this verse. Readable says what being holy means here, set apart for God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: um reino de sacerdotes e uma nação santa
decisions.reason: The phrase is kept the same at every level, as the English keeps it, so that the link with 1 Peter 2:9 (m1) shows: there the Portuguese says "nação santa" as here. Peter's "sacerdócio real" follows the Greek translation; Exodus keeps the Hebrew "reino de sacerdotes".

vi.R: Môi-se trở về và gọi những người lãnh đạo của dân đến. Ông nói cho họ biết mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho ông nói.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 와서 백성의 장로들을 불러, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 명령하신 이 모든 말씀을 그들 앞에 내놓았다.
ko.B: 모세는 돌아와 백성의 장로들을 불러 모으고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 자기에게 명령하신 이 모든 말씀을 그들 앞에 전했다.
ko.R: 모세는 돌아가서 백성의 지도자들을 불러 모았다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 전하라고 명령하신 말씀을 모두 그들에게 들려주었다.

pt.L: E Moisés veio e chamou os anciãos do povo, e pôs diante deles todas estas palavras que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe tinha ordenado.
pt.B: Moisés voltou e reuniu os anciãos do povo. Expôs diante deles todas estas palavras, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe havia ordenado.
pt.R: Moisés voltou e reuniu os líderes do povo. Contou a eles tudo o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha mandado que ele dissesse.

decisions.choice: set before them all these words: presented God's offer for their answer
decisions.reason: To "set before" someone is to lay out a choice or a word for them to respond to (Deuteronomy 11:26; 30:15). Moses does not only report; he puts the covenant offer before the people.

decisions.choice: the elders of the people: the leaders who speak for the people
decisions.reason: The elders are the heads of the tribes and families, who represent the whole people (3:16; 4:29; 12:21). Through them the message reaches everyone, and in verse 8 all the people answer.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", as elsewhere in Exodus.

source.text: וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ כָל־הָעָ֤ם יַחְדָּו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וַיָּ֧שֶׁב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered all the people together and they said, all that has spoken Yahweh we will do. And brought back Moses the words of the people to Yahweh.

en.L: And all the people answered together and said, "All that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken we will do." And Moses brought back the words of the people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The people answered as one: "We will do everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken." And Moses carried the people's words back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: All the people answered together, "We will do all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said." Then Moses went back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} what the people said.

es.L: Y respondió todo el pueblo a una y dijo: «Todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho haremos». Y Moisés llevó de vuelta las palabras del pueblo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: El pueblo respondió a una sola voz: «Haremos todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho». Y Moisés llevó la respuesta del pueblo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Todo el pueblo respondió a la vez: «Haremos todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho». Entonces Moisés volvió adonde estaba {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} contó lo que había dicho el pueblo.

fr.L: Et tout le peuple répondit ensemble et dit : « Tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit, nous le ferons. » Et Moïse rapporta les paroles du peuple {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Le peuple répondit d’une seule voix : « Nous ferons tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit. » Et Moïse porta la réponse du peuple {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Tout le peuple a répondu ensemble : « Nous ferons tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit. » Ensuite Moïse est retourné auprès {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit ce que le peuple avait répondu.

sw.L: Nao watu wote wakajibu pamoja, wakasema, "Yote aliyoyasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} tutayafanya." Naye Musa akayarudisha maneno ya watu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Watu walijibu kwa sauti moja, "Tutafanya yote ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema." Naye Musa akapeleka jibu la watu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Watu wote walijibu pamoja, "Tutafanya yote ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema." Kisha Musa akarudi kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akamweleza yale ambayo watu walisema.

vi.L: Và cả dân cùng nhau đáp lại và nói: "Mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán, chúng tôi sẽ làm." Và Môi-se đem lời của dân trình lại với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Toàn dân đồng thanh đáp: "Chúng tôi sẽ làm mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán." Môi-se đem câu trả lời của dân thưa lại với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Mọi người cùng nhau trả lời: "Chúng tôi sẽ làm mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán." Môi-se trở lại với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} những gì dân chúng đã nói.

ko.L: 그러자 온 백성이 함께 대답하여 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 모든 것을 우리가 행하겠습니다." 그리고 모세가 백성의 말을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 전해 드렸다.
ko.B: 온 백성이 한목소리로 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 것을 우리가 모두 행하겠습니다." 모세는 백성의 말을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 전해 드렸다.
ko.R: 모든 백성이 다 함께 대답했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 것을 우리가 다 하겠습니다." 그러자 모세가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 다시 올라가서 백성이 한 말을 그분께 말씀드렸다.

pt.L: E todo o povo respondeu junto e disse: "Tudo o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou faremos." E Moisés levou de volta as palavras do povo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}.
pt.B: O povo respondeu a uma só voz: "Faremos tudo o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou." E Moisés levou de volta {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} as palavras do povo.
pt.R: Todo o povo respondeu junto: "Vamos fazer tudo o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse." Então Moisés voltou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e contou a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} o que o povo tinha dito.

decisions.choice: together: all as one, with one voice
decisions.reason: The word stresses that the answer was shared by the whole people. The same promise is made again when the covenant is sealed (24:3, 7).

decisions.choice: all that Yahweh has spoken we will do: the people accept the covenant offer
decisions.reason: The people agree to the condition of verse 5 before they have heard the laws in full. Their promise will soon be tested (32:1-8).

decisions.choice: brought back the words: reported the answer
decisions.reason: Moses goes between God and the people, carrying God's word to them and their answer back to God.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י בָּ֣א אֵלֶיךָ֮ בְּעַ֣ב הֶֽעָנָן֒ בַּעֲב֞וּר יִשְׁמַ֤ע הָעָם֙ בְּדַבְּרִ֣י עִמָּ֔ךְ וְגַם־בְּךָ֖ יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַיַּגֵּ֥ד מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, look I [am] coming to you in [the] thickness of the cloud, so that may hear the people when I speak with you and also in you they will believe forever. And told Moses the words of the people to Yahweh.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Look, I [am] coming to you in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe in you forever." And Moses told the words of the people to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Look, I am coming to you in a dark, heavy cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you and will trust you from now on." Moses reported the people's words to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I will come to you in a thick, dark cloud. The people will hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} talking with you, and then they will always trust you." Moses passed on the people's answer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Mira, yo vengo a ti en lo espeso de la nube, para que el pueblo oiga cuando yo hable contigo, y también crea en ti para siempre». Y Moisés refirió las palabras del pueblo {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Mira, voy a venir a ti en una nube oscura y densa, para que el pueblo oiga cuando hable contigo y confíe en ti de ahora en adelante». Moisés comunicó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} las palabras del pueblo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Vendré a ti en una nube espesa y oscura. El pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} oirá hablar contigo, y entonces siempre confiará en ti». Moisés le transmitió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} la respuesta del pueblo.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Voici, je viens vers toi dans l’épaisseur de la nuée, afin que le peuple entende quand je parlerai avec toi, et qu’il croie aussi en toi pour toujours. » Et Moïse rapporta les paroles du peuple {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Voici, je vais venir vers toi dans une nuée sombre et épaisse, pour que le peuple entende quand je parlerai avec toi, et qu’il te fasse confiance désormais. » Moïse transmit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} les paroles du peuple.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Je vais venir vers toi dans un nuage épais et sombre. Le peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}entendra parler avec toi, et alors il te fera toujours confiance. » Moïse a transmis {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} la réponse du peuple.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninakuja kwako katika wingu zito, ili watu wasikie ninaposema nawe, na pia wakuamini wewe milele." Naye Musa akamweleza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} maneno ya watu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Tazama, ninakuja kwako katika wingu jeusi na zito, ili watu wasikie ninapozungumza nawe, nao wakuamini tangu sasa." Musa akamweleza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} maneno ya watu.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Nitakujia katika wingu zito na jeusi. Watu watanisikia nikizungumza nawe, kisha watakuamini siku zote." Musa akampelekea {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} jibu la watu.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến với ngươi trong đám mây dày đặc, để dân nghe khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với ngươi, và cũng tin ngươi mãi mãi." Và Môi-se thuật lại lời của dân với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đến với con trong một đám mây dày đặc, để dân chúng nghe khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với con, và từ nay họ sẽ luôn tin cậy con." Môi-se thưa lại với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} những lời của dân.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Ta sẽ đến với con trong một đám mây tối và dày. Dân chúng sẽ nghe {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với con, và rồi họ sẽ luôn luôn tin cậy con." Môi-se thưa lại với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} câu trả lời của dân chúng.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 내가 짙은 구름 속에서 너에게 오겠다. 내가 너와 말할 때 백성이 듣고, 또 너를 영원히 믿게 하려는 것이다." 그리고 모세가 백성의 말을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 전해 드렸다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 내가 짙고 어두운 구름 속에서 너에게 가겠다. 내가 너와 말하는 것을 백성이 듣고, 이제부터 너를 믿게 하려는 것이다." 모세는 백성의 말을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 아뢰었다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 짙고 어두운 구름 속에서 너에게 가겠다. 백성은 내가 너와 이야기하는 것을 들을 것이다. 그러면 그들이 언제나 너를 믿을 것이다." 모세는 백성의 대답을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 전해 드렸다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Eis que eu venho a ti na espessura da nuvem, para que o povo ouça quando eu falar contigo, e também creia em ti para sempre." E Moisés relatou as palavras do povo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Olha, eu venho a ti numa nuvem escura e densa, para que o povo ouça quando eu falar contigo e passe a confiar em ti daqui em diante." Moisés comunicou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} as palavras do povo.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Eu virei até ti numa nuvem escura e espessa. O povo vai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouvir falando contigo, e então sempre vai confiar em ti." Moisés transmitiu {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} a resposta do povo.

decisions.choice: the thickness of the cloud: a dense, dark cloud
decisions.reason: The first word means a thick or dark cloud, so the phrase stresses how dense it is. God comes hidden in it; the people will hear him but not see him (20:21; Deuteronomy 4:11-12).

decisions.choice: also believe in you forever: trust Moses as God's messenger from then on
decisions.reason: Hearing God speak with Moses will show the people that Moses truly speaks for God, so that they rely on his word in later times. After the sea they "believed in the LORD and in Moses his servant" (14:31).

decisions.choice: Moses told the words of the people: a repeated report
decisions.reason: Verse 8 has already said that Moses brought the people's answer back. This may repeat that report as the setting for God's reply, or it may be a second report after God's word in this verse.

decisions.choice: consecrate them: make them holy, ready to come near God
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to set apart as holy. Here it means preparing the people to be near God's presence: washing their clothes and keeping from sexual relations (verses 14-15; Genesis 35:2; Joshua 3:5).

decisions.choice: wash their clothes: an outward sign of being made ready
decisions.reason: Washing the clothes before meeting God shows that the people are clean and set apart (Genesis 35:2; Leviticus 15). The washing is a sign; the holiness comes from God's call.

decisions.choice: make them holy and ready to meet with me
decisions.reason: Readable explains "consecrate" with its purpose here, which verses 11 and 17 make clear.

decisions.choice: "consacrer" for the piel of qadash
decisions.reason: "Consacrer" says plainly that the people are set apart and made ready to come near God; "sanctifier" suggests moral holiness more than the rite of preparation described in verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: "uwatakase" (make them holy) for consecrate
decisions.reason: "Kutakasa" is the usual verb for making people holy and clean before God; "kuweka wakfu" is used more for setting apart things and offerings.

decisions.choice: "거룩하게 하다" (L, R); "거룩하게 구별하다" (B)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for holy; Balanced adds "구별하다", as Joshua in Korean does, to show that consecrating sets people apart for God.

decisions.choice: "thánh hóa" (L, B); "làm cho họ nên thánh" (R)
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to make holy, ready to come near God (meaning decision); "thánh hóa" is the short word, and Readable says it plainly with "thánh", the term sheet's word for holy.

decisions.choice: consagrar
decisions.reason: "Consagrar" is to set apart as holy (m1), the word Portuguese uses for preparing people and things for God; "santificar" can suggest making someone morally holy, which is more than the washing and keeping apart of verses 14-15. Readable says "tornar santo", as the English Readable says "make holy".

decisions.choice: set bounds for the people all around: mark a limit around the mountain that the people may not pass
decisions.reason: The verb means to set a border. The limit keeps the people back; in verse 23 Moses speaks of it as setting bounds for the mountain itself. Both are true: the line runs around the mountain and holds the people off.

decisions.choice: its edge: the lowest slopes, the foot of the mountain
decisions.reason: The word means the end or edge of something. Here it is the place where the mountain begins. Even touching it is forbidden while God is present on it.

decisions.choice: shall surely be put to death: the mountain is holy while God is on it
decisions.reason: The doubled verb is the form used in the law for the death penalty (21:12). The mountain has become holy ground (3:5), and crossing the limit is treated as a capital offense.

decisions.choice: a line all around the mountain that the people must not cross
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "set bounds for the people all around" means.

decisions.choice: The command passed to the people in 해라체 ("-하라", "-하지 마라") with the death penalty in the plain written style ("죽여야 한다")
decisions.reason: The term sheet sets 해라체 for God's commands and the plain written style for third-person law; these hold through the laws of chapters 20-23.

decisions.choice: "chớ" (L), "không được" (B), "đừng" (R) for a prohibition; "phải bị xử tử" for "shall surely be put to death"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's pattern for God's commands: "chớ" only at a terse Literal, "không được" at Balanced, "đừng" in plain Readable sentences. Recorded once for these chapters; the same pattern runs through the laws of chapters 20 to 23.

decisions.choice: certamente será morto (L); deverá ser morto (B); tem de ser morto (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, the doubled verb of the death penalty (m3; 21:12-17) is "certamente será morto" at Literal, a sentence carried out by the community, not only "morrerá"; Balanced says "deverá ser morto" and Readable "tem de ser morto", the forms the laws of chapters 21-22 also use.
